data.title: Is Wintour still en vogue? Met navigates rough seas as Galliano retrospective sinks into 'Horizons'
data.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Dana Thomas, author of Gods and Kings: The Rise and Fall of Alexander McQueen and John Galliano and the New York Times bestseller Deluxe: How Luxury Lost Its Luster. The fiery controversy surrounding the Met’s now-cancelled John Galliano retrospective revives the timeless debate over whether we can separate the art from the artist. But our guest argues that the central issue is one of institutional power, with the art itself almost relegated to an afterthought. From her perspective, Galliano’s stature as an artist and fashion designer was never in dispute. His character, however, is once again being called into question in a very public arena.

data.title: US-Iran war: Old videos falsely claim to show new attacks on American bases
data.description: As US-Iran hostilities flare up and strikes has resumed, so has a wave of misinformation online. Old and unrelated videos are flooding social media, falsely presented as footage of new attacks. data.title: ‘I don’t chase the dollar. I never did’: the astonishing hidden life of Mr T

At 74, he rarely gives interviews. But when Mr T decides to talk, he really does talk. What Mr T thinks, Mr T says. And I’ve never heard anyone trash the very thing they’re here to promote quite like Mr T does today. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘My work has always been serious’: Maurizio Cattelan on his $6m banana, his gold toilet – and bringing Hitler and a pope to Berlin
data.description: He is famed for creating a golden loo that was stolen and a $6m banana that was eaten. But, says the sculptor ahead of a major new show in Germany, there’s more to his work than pranks and provocation Maurizio Cattelan, the art world’s merriest prankster, pauses when asked which object in his sprawling new Berlin show is most likely to be defaced, stolen or eaten, then emits a foghorn of a laugh. “There is no need to vandalise anything,” says the trim, soulful Italian, explaining that he has already taken care of all that, given how the work cuts villains, imposters and straw men down to size. “But,” he says, referring to the show’s more daring works, “maybe we need someone to resuscitate people.” Cattelan, who speaks in a lilting English, grins broadly, a mischievous glint in his brown eyes. Speaking on the subterranean level of Mies van der Rohe’s weightless Neue Nationalgalerie (NNG) in Berlin, he darts between the impish and the profound in conversation, mirroring the dizzying range of his work. The silver-haired sculptor is best known for duct-taping a banana to a wall in 2019 and calling it Comedian, in a droll commentary on the excesses of the art market. The joke became even funnier when it sold for $6.2m, then hilarious when its buyer took a bite out of his purchase and swallowed it . Continue reading...

data.title: The people of France are in an extraordinary funk about their future – here’s why | Paul Taylor
data.description: The race to succeed Emmanuel Macron is looming, but rarely has the mood been so gloomy or the lure of extremist solutions so alarming France, as the French travel writer Sylvain Tesson once noted, “is a paradise inhabited by people who think they live in hell”. As the campaign for next year’s presidential election hits its stride with ever more wannabes declaring their candidacies, the country is in a particularly sullen mood. If the vote were held now, the anti-immigration populist Marine Le Pen would have a strong chance of romping into the Élysée palace, riding a wave of voter disillusionment with the entire political class and a sense that “we’ve tried everything else”. But a lot can happen between now and 18 April 2027, the date of the first round. France is also a country of sudden shocks. Paul Taylor is a senior visiting fellow at the European Policy Centre Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A crisis of authenticity’: the truth about food influencers
data.description: Instagrammers have upended the British restaurant scene, and amassed followings in the millions. But has their moment already passed? In 2017, two aspiring YouTubers going by the name Topjaw published a video posing the London foodie’s most important question: what to eat in Chinatown ? They enlisted the help of longtime Instagrammer Kar-Shing Tong (better known by his username @ks_ate_here ), who took them on a lovingly curated loop of the neighbourhood. Cantonese siu mei duck at Four Seasons, Chongqing-style handmade noodles at the now defunct Little Wooden Hut, and Barshu on Frith Street, where they decadently cracked a whole crab for the camera. Any of the 100,000-odd viewers who watched it at the time would be well served by its responsible (if unspectacular) recommendations. But in retrospect, the video may be of more interest to historians. In its unassuming and rapidly cut seven minutes, you can almost see the tectonic plates of the food world begin to shift. Tong is the elder statesman: the @ks_ate_here account began in the social media dark ages, first on Twitter then on an Instagram that was dominated by static photography. He’s in his element in the video, dutifully explaining the history and technique behind the dishes. He is relaxed and affable in front of the camera, but in his own work he doesn’t show his face often – it just wasn’t the style. Topjaw is something different. Nine years ago, it was still embryonic: host Jesse Burgess sweating profusely at any hint of chilli, cameraman Will Warr unable to use chopsticks. But the formula was there. The constant checking in to see if what they’re eating truly is “the best”. Even doubled over from the heat of a spicy fish soup, Burgess’s eyes always find the camera. He holds out food for inspection and addresses the imagined viewer. The audience is out there. “KS has 40,000 Instagram followers! 40,000!” Burgess says, pointing at Tong with aspirational glee. Continue reading...

data.title: Is Ulrich Siegmund the most dangerous man in Germany? - podcast
data.description: Ulrich Siegmund, the charismatic young leader of the AfD party in Saxony-Anhalt, has been labelled Germany’s most dangerous man by Der Spiegel. John Kampfner explains why The German news magazine Der Spiegel has long had a taste for provocation. But one of its cover stories last month really captured people’s attention. It carried a picture of a young east German politician called Ulrich Siegmund. He looked pretty good, his chin covered with designer stubble, his hair combed into a neat quiff, his green eyes staring right into the camera, under the headline “ Der gefährlichste Mann Deutschlands ”: Germany’s most dangerous man. You might think Siegmund would hate that Spiegel cover. Far from it. On the campaign trail in recent weeks he has been autographing copies: he even filmed himself signing one for his 800,000 TikTok followers. If the polls are correct, Siegmund could soon become the first far-right leader of a German state since Adolf Hitler’s time. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Supersizing before our eyes’: UN warns of record El Niño approaching
data.description: Event is likely to be largest in at least 1,000 years and will pile extra heat into a world already in a climate crisis The El Niño climate phenomenon is “supersizing before our eyes”, the UN has said. The event is near certain to shatter temperature records, according to the latest forecasts. The El Niño is likely to be the largest in at least 1,000 years and will pile extra heat into an atmosphere where temperatures are already rising rapidly due to global heating. The combination means 2027 is set to “ blow apart ” the record and be the hottest year ever recorded . Continue reading...

data.title: Labour party of ‘big money’, claims Greens’ Polanski as he says he will run for Starmer’s seat – UK politics live
data.description: Green party leader announces run in Holborn and St Pancras constituency in north London following the resignation of former PM Full report: Zack Polanski to stand in Keir Starmer seat as Green party candidate These are from Rob Ford , a politics professor and elections specialist, on what Zack Polanski being the Green party’s candidate means for the Holborn and St Pancras byelection. Big stakes now for both parties. Greens have chance to turn the tide on recent decline & show Polanski is a winner. As I said a couple of days ago, Polanski candidature may change how voters in the seat see contest. No longer just Green vs Lab - it is now “would you like the national leader of the Green party or a generic Lab backbencher as your local representative?” It is quite possible for Labour to lose despite being popular nationally and, indeed, in seat itself, because voters understand stakes: Green gain still leaves Burnham in charge with huge majority, but means a high profile progressive voice in Commons, representing Holborn & St P If you are a young progressive voter who thinks “I like Burnham but I don’t trust him to listen to us, particularly given how the first two yrs of this govt went”, then a “vote Polanski in to keep Burnham honest” message is going to be quite attractive. There are an awful lot of such voters in this seat - lots of students & young grad professionals (seat is v near UCL), & lots of migrant origin & ethnic minority voters too. data.title: The place that never freezes: the Arctic habitat where global heating threatens more ice, not less
data.description: The race to study the North Water between Canada and Greenland before it changes has led to a bold plan for an Inuit-run protected area Electric-blue meltwater sprays up under Terry Noah’s snowmobile as he races across sea ice extending out from Canada’s northernmost public community: Grise Fiord in Nunavut, a hamlet of 144 people closer to Murmansk in Russia than the Canadian city of Toronto. The bay’s cliffs loom higher and higher like stone icebergs as he approaches his destination across the bay. Noah pulls his sled carefully over a seal’s breathing hole, about the circumference of a basketball. Using a custom-made winch, he lowers a submersible instrument into the sea below the ice. data.title: A Death of One’s Own by Terry Eagleton review – meditations on arriving at a full stop
data.description: The literary critic brings his vast reading to bear on life’s most inescapable fact Terry Eagleton is not a fan of sloppy thinking, especially when it comes to the granite fact of death. He particularly doesn’t like the attitude of Dylan Thomas who famously urged his ailing father to “not go gentle into that good night”. If the “night” – death – is so “good” then why, asks Eagleton reasonably, would Thomas want his dad to dawdle? Shouldn’t DJ Thomas, rather, be encouraged to trot towards his lovely end like an ecstatic marathon runner on the home straight? Eagleton’s reproach to Thomas’s doublethink should not be read as panicky denial about the reality of his own mortality. To the contrary, Eagleton, who at 83 admits that he wasn’t sure whether this book would end up being published posthumously, finds it hard to think or write about much else. After a 60-year academic career spent tussling with Marxist literary theory, not to mention the epistemological void at the heart of postmodernism criticism, these days Eagleton is more interested in pondering death and how it “lacks a sense of occasion”. It might visit, for example, while you happen to be dressed in a giraffe outfit. Continue reading...

data.title: I camped in one of Britain’s last remaining rainforests
data.description: A fragment of temperate rainforest lies on the edge of Dartmoor, and following years of conservation work, its owners have now opened up a sustainable campsite next to this fragile ecosystem Mist blankets the valley as I wheel my camping gear down the small hill towards a clearing ringed by trees and shrubs. A picnic bench sits at its edge, angled towards the reason why I’m here: one of the last remaining fragments of temperate rainforest in Britain. I’m pitching my tent at Wray Valley Camping, a low-impact site on Dartmoor’s eastern edge between Lustleigh and Moretonhampstead, where I’ll spend five days on one of the site’s “nearly wild” pitches. Also known as Atlantic woodland, temperate rainforests depend on a rare combination of high humidity, rainfall and consistently mild coastal temperatures where the sea moderates the climate. They once stretched from the western Highlands of Scotland down to Cornwall, covering 20% of the UK , and sheltering rare and delicate lichens and plants. Today more than 95% of our temperate rainforest cover is gone, but Devon’s near-constant dampness and its exposure to the Atlantic make it one of the last strongholds for this rare habitat. data.title: New musical to give intimate portrait of Marilyn Monroe and Arthur Miller’s marriage
data.description: Misfits Together, by Bastille’s Dan Smith and To Kill a King’s Ralph Pelleymounter, is set amid the 1950s’ ‘red scare’ It was lampooned as the union of the “hourglass” and the “egghead” – the marriage, in the summer of 1956, between Hollywood superstar Marilyn Monroe and Pulitzer-winning playwright Arthur Miller. Now, a new stage musical is to give a nuanced and intimate portrait of that famous relationship, treat each as trailblazers in their own way and reveal parallels between the volatile state of the US during the 50s “red scare” and now. The production, which opens next autumn at Leicester’s Curve , is called Misfits Together, a reference to the film Miller wrote for Monroe that was released shortly after their divorce in 1961. It is a foray into musical theatre by two indie musicians, Dan Smith of the band Bastille and Ralph Pelleymounter from To Kill a King, who have recorded the score as a studio album. The first track, Oh America, is out on Thursday. Continue reading...

data.title: The Gentlemen season two review – these geezers in tweed are irritating, stupid and extremely funny
data.description: Guy Ritchie’s crime caper is back with the usual hijinks, swearing and men shaking their fists. But its ridiculousness is strangely comforting – and Theo James’s beefcake Eddie is so bland that he is fascinating to observe He lives in a house, a very big house in the country. He has pectorals the size of Bentleys and wears plus-fours so voluminous they could accommodate his fleet of gundogs and still provide room for snarling groundskeeper Geoff (“I would do anyfink for you an’ this famlee”). And yet! Edward “Eddie” Horniman, 13th Duke of Halstead (Theo James), is sad. And aggrieved. A moment’s silence, please, as this powerful hunk pontificates on the unbearable lightness of being the millionaire protagonist in Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen. “Four hundred years ago, this estate spread out as far as the eye could see,” he tells Geoff (Vinnie Jones) as the camera swoops over his verdant playpen, a lavish patchwork of abundant hedges and cap-doffing deer. “But it’s been diminished. Year after year. Generation after generation. First came the apologies, then came the shame, then came the contraction. I want it back, Geoff,” he growls, hexagonal jaw stiff with emotion. “I want it all back!” Continue reading...

data.title: The September reset is real. I’m about to become a better person, flaxseed by flaxseed | Emma Brockes
data.description: Small changes are what I’m aiming for – 10-minute workouts, cleaning out my handbag. Then I’m less likely to have failed come October Are you a January resolutions or a September reset person? The latter has always felt more propitious to me, light of the exhaustion of Christmas and with the weather still on our side. Last week, when the Pavlovian response to buying new stationery (for my kids) kicked in, I found myself following a rote impulse to sort my life out by replacing the bag in the vacuum cleaner and committing to an unsustainable course of personal change. This is it! The beginning of a new way of life, driven by sharp pencils and the crispness of autumn. I mean, it won’t last. But while most of us have read enough advisories cautioning against new year resolutions as durable, somehow September still promises the earth. I can’t shake it. As soon as the breeze picks up and the leaves start to turn, I feel my pilot light ignite – and the urge to sign up to unaffordable personal training sets in. It feels like an ancient response. I’m not writing this while leaning on a dry stone wall or managing my sheepdogs, but still; the sensory changes brought in by autumn surely activate latent energies in all of us. If you can avoid pumpkin spice and survive the costume search for Halloween, September triggers good feelings of renewal via the psychic memory of our serf forebears bringing in the harvest. Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: China’s demise was gleefully predicted by the west – meanwhile, it built an AI revolution | Larry Elliott
data.description: Free AI models that are as good as the investment-hungry US versions will disrupt global markets, and offer Britain a lesson Almost from the moment it began, the end of the Chinese economic miracle has been much anticipated. Thick and fast, the books have come explaining how it will end badly. Overinvestment. A country wallowing in debt. The collapse of the property market . Political repression. The demand for democracy from a growing middle class. All have been put forward as reasons for the inevitable terminal crisis. Even those impressed by the country’s rapid growth took comfort from the notion that the west would continue to dominate advanced manufacturing while China would be stuck assembling TVs. And while the wait for its much-predicted demise has gone on and on, China has become the workshop of the world. Larry Elliott is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Israeli settlements: Britain can no longer look away | Editorial
data.description: International law, European action and UK public opinion point the same way. Britain should stop helping to sustain Israeli settlements economically In the Commons this week, the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, appeared to have accepted the principle of a trade ban between the UK and Israeli settlements, which Britain says are illegal under international law. This is long overdue. The test now is whether his promised “ comprehensive reset ” deserves the name. Stopping settlement-produced goods at the border is not enough. Britain should prohibit its companies from sustaining settlement activity – by financing, constructing, insuring, advertising – in territory whose occupation it regards as unlawful. The ban must have teeth. The UK can no longer ignore the violence and pressure exerted on Palestinians in the West Bank by Israel’s government, military and settlers. There have been more than 1,400 settler attacks so far this year, according to the UN, against a record 1,800 registered in 2025. An election campaign has only made matters worse. Last month, Israel issued tenders for 1,234 homes in the 3,401 -unit E1 development east of Jerusalem. The country’s ministers gave the green light for the controversial settlement – long condemned for effectively bisecting the West Bank – expressly to “ erase ” the idea of a Palestinian state, the creation of which the UK officially supports. data.title: Premier League paradox: midfielders are more and more expensive, yet more and more mediocre | Jonathan Liew
data.description: Enzo Fernández and Sandro Tonali had big-money summer moves, but can they hold a candle to past greats? Perhaps the only thing you really need to know about the modern midfield role is that Enzo Maresca reckons that Marc Guéhi can play it better than Mateo Kovacic. Guéhi, in reality a centre-back, started the season in midfield for Manchester City, ahead of Kovacic, the now-departed Nico González, and Matheus Nunes. In this context City’s purchase of Enzo Fernández for a club record £125m can be seen in one of two ways: either an enormous statement of intent, or a hell of a lot of money to pay for Guéhi’s understudy. We jest, of course. Fernández is in fact a very different kind of midfielder to Guéhi, largely on the basis that he actually is a midfielder. Versatile, able to receive deep from the goalkeeper or the centre-halves; capable of recycling or progressing the ball in tight spots, driving into final-third positions as a No 8, ghosting into the penalty area and offering an advanced goal threat. Like Elliot Anderson, signed from Nottingham Forest for £116m but so long ago that in transfer window time it no longer counts, Fernández is one of the new breed of Premier League central midfielders who seems to offer everything; albeit in modest qualities, and whose primary attribute appears to be the absence of exposed risk he represents. Versatile, able to receive deep from the goalkeeper or the centre-halves; capable of recycling or progressing the ball in tight spots, driving into final-third positions as a No 8, ghosting into the penalty area and offering an advanced goal threat. Like Elliot Anderson, signed from Nottingham Forest for £116m but so long ago that in transfer window time it no longer counts, Fernández is one of the new breed of Premier League central midfielders who seems to offer everything; albeit in modest qualities, and whose primary attribute appears to be the absence of exposed risk he represents. data.title: Katie Taylor finally gets her ‘fairytale ending’ with Croke Park homecoming
data.description: Irish fight legend can cap a special career by retiring as the undisputed super-lightweight champion with victory against Flora Pili on Saturday “I won’t be like Tyson Fury, coming back again and again,” Katie Taylor told me with a little smile a few years ago as she explained how, when she finally retired, she would leave boxing for good. The moment is almost here because, on Saturday night, in front of 80,000 fans at a fevered Croke Park, Taylor will fight for the very last time . She will depart as a quietly defiant pioneer and an overwhelming force for good – both in Ireland and women’s boxing. The fight game is full of heartbreak and broken promises, corruption and damage, but it also produces singular characters who elevate the world. Joe Louis in the 1930s, and Muhammad Ali in the 1960s, had a profound impact on American society. In a very different world today, Oleksandr Usyk is also more than a boxer. He remains an inspiration and a source of undimmed hope in wartime Ukraine. Continue reading...

data.title: Katie Boulter crashes out of US Open after Karolina Muchova nightmare

data.title: China’s falling emissions amid Iran war spark hope of decarbonisation watershed
data.description: Oil consumption plummets and EV sales soar as analysts say demand may not fully return even if crude price falls China’s carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% after the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran, thanks to a sharp reduction in oil consumption and a steady rise in the use of electric vehicles and public transport, analysis shows. The report reveals the role of clean energy in cushioning the price shocks caused by the strait of Hormuz crisis to the world’s biggest oil importer. It also reinforces hopes that China, which is the world’s biggest greenhouse gas emitter, may be nearing a turning point in decarbonising its economy. Continue reading...

data.title: Why El Niño can mean less rain but heavier downpours for India
data.description: El Niño is associated with weaker monsoons in India – but research suggests it can also bring more extreme rainfall The world is bracing for a “super” El Niño, and its effects are already being felt in India, where the monsoon has brought less rain than average but more intense downpours. Meteorologists predict that the current El Niño , which is developing over the Pacific, could be one of the strongest in living memory. India is likely to be heavily affected, particularly later in the monsoon, when El Niño’s influence tends to strengthen. Continue reading...

data.title: Patagonia sues Trump over slashing of protected areas in Utah
data.description: President’s order strips nearly 3m acres of Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante, sacred tribal sites, of safeguards Patagonia, the outdoor clothing and gear company, has joined a lawsuit challenging Donald Trump’s decision to significantly reduce the Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments in Utah, removing protections from nearly 3m acres. In July, the president approved the reduction of the sites by 90%, clearing the way to open the land to oil and gas companies. He argued in his proclamations that doing so would allow lands to be “put to a higher-priority use” and that they contained critical minerals important to “resource independence …[and] national security”. data.title: ‘I show how energetic it can be’: the photographer capturing Britain’s golden age of jazz
data.description: Temi Adegbayibi started out taking pictures of the Ezra Collective and other British musicians as a hobby, then found his work exhibited at the Royal Albert Hall. He discusses Black joy and the movement and stillness of jazz When I speak to Temi Adegbayibi on the phone, the 26-year-old photographer is on the move. He is travelling across London, then running up the stairs to his desk, fitting our conversation into the interstitial spaces of a life split between freelance photography, film production and working at the Royal Albert Hall. His glittering portfolio includes photographs of Jorja Smith, Basement Jaxx, Fireboy DML and Ezra Collective, but like many in the creative industries, he oscillates between the glamour of the stage and the reality of making a living. “I’ve always had day jobs,” he says. “Most photographers back in the day weren’t shooting for money, they were shooting for passion.” Continue reading...

data.title: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home review – Kirk, Spock and co on semi-intentionally hilarious save-the-whale mission
data.description: Our heroes travel back through time to San Francisco in 1986 so they can commune with aliens threatening future Earth – it’s preposterously good fun Here is the fourth and silliest movie in the Star Trek franchise, now on rerelease for its 40th anniversary. Directed by Leonard Nimoy, it’s a film of pure shark-jumping or rather whale-jumping absurdity. The film’s opening credits proclaim, with sublime confidence in its own unquestioned pop-cultural importance in the field of space travel, that Star Trek IV is dedicated to the crew of the space shuttle Challenger, which had that year catastrophically exploded midair, killing all seven of them. Spock has been brought back to life, as the apparent end result of all the bizarre metempsychotic plot contortions of the previous film. But the permanent and irrevocable death of Kirk’s son seems to be passed over remarkably casually. The eerie boyishness of Shatner’s Kirk, with that beaming smile, almost makes you forget that he has been through an agonising bereavement. Hasn’t he? Continue reading...

data.title: Stolen Babies review – the scale of this cruelty is almost impossible to fathom
data.description: For decades, thousands of unmarried mothers in the UK were forced to give up their newborns after being denied pain relief in labour so they would ‘not be a bad girl again’. This harrowing documentary hears their stories The scale of the suffering at first threatens to make you numb to it. The 90-minute documentary Stolen Babies is as unsparing as it is unsentimental and opens with a bald statement of verified fact: “Between 1949 and 1976 over 250,000 unmarried mothers in the UK were forced into handing their newborn babies over for adoption.” State apparatus facilitated this every step of the way, supported by religious institutions. These institutions ran, or were involved with running, the mother and baby homes to which the girls and young women were banished (“They do not quickly acknowledge themselves as sinners,” notes one report on its inmates), along with self-proclaimed moral welfare societies and the NHS. The statistics are appalling. The details are worse. Some of the women whose stories are told in the film became pregnant by boyfriends. Some were victims of rape. Joan Chambers was 14 when a teacher took her for a walk in the woods. “I trusted him, I really did … All I remember was the pain. I honestly didn’t know what was happening.” Continue reading...

data.title: Lomu review – fascinatingly nuanced tribute to rugby’s first superstar
data.description: His destructive pace and power changed the game for ever, but behind the fame and ineffable exterior of this gentle giant was a life of chaos and emotional discord There’s an inevitable air of melancholy overhanging this profile of New Zealand rugby star Jonah Lomu; we all know how the story ended for this magnificent human specimen, who died in 2015 aged 40 as a result of a longterm kidney disorder. Lomu, of course, became a legend of the game after breaking into the All Blacks side – the ferociously high-achieving New Zealand national team, for anyone outside the rugby-appreciating universe – at the scarcely believable age of 19; his special combination of a tank-like physique, electric pace and ability to slalom at high speed gave him an almost unstoppable force in what is arguably the toughest contact sport of all. Lomu had the bulk and power of a forward (I liked the detail that he was sometimes drafted into the back of the scrum when they needed “more power”) but he was set loose on the wing, where he was twice the speed and three times the size of everyone else, and where his destructive instincts could wreak havoc. Well, modern rugby appears to have learned the Lomu lesson; everyone has bulked up – so its arguable whether he would have the same impact today. But as this film underlines, there was a lot more to Lomu’s story than steamrolling the hapless English backline; he had a complicated relationship both with his Tongan heritage and his superstar status, the combination of which seemed to overwhelm him. Interestingly, this film (directed by Gavin Fitzgerald and Vea Mafile’o) initially appears to push the by-now customary idea that Lomu’s Indigenous heritage was an ineffable source of strength, wisdom and insight; however it soon becomes clear that this wasn’t entirely the case. Continue reading...

data.title: Ink review – Danny Boyle turns the birth of the Sun into a lurid tabloid frenzy
data.description: Venice film festival Jack O’Connell is terrific as editor Larry Lamb in James Graham’s tale of Rupert Murdoch, Page 3 and the newspaper that transformed Fleet Street Danny Boyle presents us with a lurid, violent and thumpingly unsubtle movie full of Dutch angles, cartoony shocks and gargoyle closeups. It’s a chapter in the prehistory of modern media, adapted by James Graham from his 2017 stage play , filled with shame and fear and self-hate. It is in fact the story of the Sun newspaper, and how Rupert Murdoch (Guy Pearce) bought the ailing minor title in the late 60s and hired a tough Yorkshire newspaperman, Larry Lamb, to turn it into a raucous and gleefully vulgar circulation powerhouse. Ink summons up the energy and frenzy of tabloid papers of the era, but also – and not entirely intentionally – how strangely depressing they were. Audiences used to the super-rich anomie of the Roy family from TV’s Succession might find all this very unsexy. This is a world of officer-class Fleet Street execs having expense-account meals at Rules and the Savoy Grill in pinstripe suits, smoking and drinking and impassively writing salary offers on paper napkins and silently passing them across to each other. Meanwhile, the other ranks of journalists and print unions are covered in sweat and ink. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Everything countercultural is doomed, isn’t it?’​ Sofie Royer, the bracingly brilliant pop star pondering life’s big questions
data.description: Referencing Tarkovsky and French theory, the Austrian-Iranian singer is writing some of today’s wittiest music – though she’s ‘too pop for the art world, too indie-darling for the mainstream’ You wait ages for a brilliant pop song about film-making and then two come along at once. Following on from Charli xcx’s Camera comes Actress by Sofie Royer, with lyrics referencing rotoscoping, call sheets, screenplays, establishing shots, cinéma verité and more. “When the dust settles on your heart / I’d like to audition for the leading part,” she purrs over pumping disco, screwball-funny as she stacks up the metaphors to woo some Letterboxd-brained beau. “My mise-en-scène is flawless, don’t you know I’m quite adored / I’ll win you over in 35mm 4K-restored.” It’s a typically smart and witty number from a singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and, as it happens, aspiring actor, whose erudition and taste light up one of the best albums of the year, the forthcoming Before/After. Its lead single Cowboy Mouth is a recreation of a Sam Shepard play in song; another song makes a catchy funk-pop chorus from the word “sesquicentennial”. Her music is cosmopolitan enough to sit Italo disco next to new wave and garage rock, and across her discography there’s a big cast of cultural figures from Andrei Tarkovsky to Kenneth Anger, Luigi Mangione to Ivy Wolk, knowingness offset by her keen sense of humour. Continue reading...

data.title: Chasing Freedom: a poignant reflection on empire, education and parental expectations
data.description: Simukai Chigudu’s filmic memoir details the confines and conflicts of growing up in Zimbabwe during political turmoil. Don’t already get The Long Wave in your inbox? Sign up here Last week, I finally managed to snatch one read out of the jaws of a hectic summer. On a series of very long-haul flights (highly recommended as a way to break reading droughts), I fell into the world of Simukai Chigudu’s Chasing Freedom: Coming of Age at the End of Empire. I finished the book just as I was landing in Nairobi, Kenya. In a daze, I stepped on to the tarmac in the chill of equatorial winter. The book was about growing up in post-colonial Zimbabwe and navigating life between the ex-colonised and the ex-colonial power. But the account of Chigudu’s life also captured, in ways that sometimes left me breathless with the shock of recognition, what felt like a broader shared experience for those of us born to parents whose traumas we never understood. This week, I reflected on how Chigudu’s experience connects to that of a wider post-colonial African generation. Continue reading...

data.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a phenomenon – but there is much more to the gaming world
data.description: As Rockstar’s blockbuster prepares to dominate the headlines, it’s time for the mainstream media to stop treating video games as a novelty that needs explaining Predictably, the Grand Theft Auto VI “extended look” which premiered on Netflix last week was a success for all involved. The 30-minute preview scorched to No 1 on the viewing chart and even brought the site down for a few minutes as millions of gamers tried to watch what was, effectively, a very long teaser trailer. According to data collated by Eurogamer , more than 9,000 Twitch streamers covered the show leading to 5,227,798 hours of viewing there alone. And this was just the beginning of what will surely be two months of escalating hype – and unprecedented media attention. Call me cynical, but I suspect the coverage of GTA VI in the media over the next few weeks will follow a familiar pattern. Mostly, it will be five-minute slots wedged in near the end of news bulletins in which games journalists, industry analysts and other pundits will be asked why the game is such a big deal, how much it cost to make and how much revenue it will generate. Perhaps a few will try to reignite the hoary old “violence in video games” debate, there will be presenters laughingly admitting they’ve not touched a game since Pac-Man, rolling their eyes and wallowing in their ignorance, in a way they never would while discussing any other art form. Somebody will venture the subversive view that “games are no longer just for kids”; somebody else will say “games make more money than films and music put together”. And that will be that, job done for another decade … or until there’s a funny story about Pokémon. Continue reading...

data.title: Star Wars Zero Company review – joyfully absurd heroics with a tight-knit team of misfits
data.description: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S/X, PC; Bit Reactor Split priorities between scripted and emergent story moments hamper an otherwise brilliant Star Wars-themed successor to XCOM Even if you’re unfamiliar with the term “emergent storytelling”, you’ve likely experienced some of the unscripted tales that can bubble up out of a game’s systems. Perhaps you’ve led a scheming dynasty in Crusader Kings, or watched a favourite hero succumb to madness in Darkest Dungeon . Maybe you’ve surrendered yourself to the infinite yarn-spinner that is Dwarf Fortress – or read about it from the mid-00s forums where users helped popularise the term “Let’s Play” by chronicling their games in descriptive posts. Or perhaps you’ve played Firaxis’ XCOM , the alien invasion tactics hit that several key members of Zero Company studio Bit Reactor had a hand in. Zero Company hinges on a concept as simple as it is perfect: take the complementary class abilities, tough dice rolls, and permanent character deaths of XCOM, and house them in a sci-fi setting known for spaghetti western blaster duels, last stands and heroic sacrifices. As creative director Greg Foertsch puts it , “Star Wars is about loss.” Which losses you end up mourning in Zero Company depends on you. Continue reading...

data.title: Simply the best? Is the Berlin Philharmonic really better than all the rest?
data.description: The orchestra – at the Proms this week – is hailed as among the best in the world, if not the best. For my money, that’s quite possibly right, but why? The Berlin Philharmonic are in London tonight and tomorrow at the Proms , days after closing the Edinburgh international festival in thrilling style. It was their first visit to Scotland in over 20 years, but the orchestra and their chief conductor, Kirill Petrenko, are regular Proms visitors ; their Royal Albert Hall concerts are always season highlights. “The best orchestra in the world”, as it is often hailed , brings programmes that offer the expected and – for them – the unexpected. Tonight there’s Tchaikovsky’s Fourth Symphony paired with Elgar’s Enigma Variations, a piece that’s still an astoundingly rare visitor to this orchestra’s concerts; and tomorrow, the safety-first repertoire warhorse is Beethoven’s Violin Concerto, but it’s paired with Scriabin’s brilliantly unhinged Third Symphony. data.description: Over 40% of films in LFF programme are female-made, but only two of 21 gala films are directed by women Female film-makers are still being squeezed out of the industry as they progress beyond their debut films, the director of the London film festival has said, adding that “the dial does not seem to be moving”. Kristy Matheson’s comments came as LFF announced its full programme for this year’s event, which runs from 7 to 19 October. data.description: I snapped at my children. Resented daily pickup. data.title: How to turn past-their-best bananas into a glorious ice-cream – recipe | Waste not
data.description: Bananas often go off quickly, so use up over-ripe, brown specimens in a sugar-free dessert that will satisfy any sweet-tooth cravings With two young kids, we get through a lot of bananas in our household. Perhaps surprisingly, though, most of them are frozen: our daughters eat them straight from the freezer most evenings, with frozen berries and yoghurt, for pudding. We normally order a stack of bananas every Saturday, and before the end of the week they inevitably start to turn brown. At this point, we peel, slice and freeze them for the children’s evening yoghurt, though sometimes, when we have a real excess, I turn them into today’s incredibly satisfying “ice-cream”. Its silky-smooth texture really hits the spot, and satisfies any ice-cream cravings without recourse to added sugar or excessive fat. The trick is to freeze the bananas in a single layer on a flat tray, so they don’t freeze into a homogeneous mass, then transfer to a container to enjoy as and when. Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: swot up with these lessons in back-to-school dressing
data.description: September is the most fun time of year to shop, but it can also be dangerously seductive. Keep your wits about you with these tips I used to love back-to-school shopping when my children were little. The miniature highlighter pens, the name labels, those pop-out pencil cases from Smiggle, even the intergenerational wrangling over when the price of a water bottle becomes unreasonable. I love the ceremony of new beginnings. The curtain-raising drama of it all. Luckily for me, you don’t have to grow out of back-to-school shopping even though your children do, because in fashion September is considered the start of the new year. This is eminently sensible, because this time of year is a much better moment for a restart than January. The actual new year is dark and bleak and makes resolutions and projects feel intimidating rather than exciting. But right now, the evenings are still light, and while I’ve still got a bit of a tan pretty much anything feels possible. Continue reading...

data.title: I thought I was too broken for sex. Here’s how I found pleasure again
data.description: I was forced to examine the idea of sexual pleasure after a tumor was removed from my spinal cord Ten years ago, my right elbow started to hurt. The internet suggested I had tennis elbow, so I stopped playing tennis. Once the outer elbow pain moved inward, I changed my self-diagnosis to golfer’s elbow. I stopped lifting weights , competitive dragon-boating and bouldering. For good measure, I consulted an occupational therapist about my nightly bullet-vibrator routine after reading that golfer’s elbow is common among construction workers who operate heavy-duty vibrating machinery. He listened closely and said he’d note VRI on my patient chart. I asked what VRI meant, eager to end my diagnostic journey. “Vibrator-related injury,” he responded. We busted out laughing. Continue reading...

data.title: Freelancers are getting buried with ‘soulless’ AI slop cleanup: ‘It’s a shame we need to do it’
data.description: As more companies turn to AI, they’re hiring freelancers to clean up its mistakes rather than create original work Lisa, a freelance graphic designer based in Spain, noticed a shift in her work after the release of ChatGPT in 2022. She went from receiving slow one-off jobs creating logos and packaging to an onslaught of requests asking her to fix versions that were generated by artificial intelligence – from sharpening fuzzy images for printing to turning flawed designs into usable files. By 2025, Lisa, who asked not to be fully named to avoid solicitations, said 90% of her incoming logo and packaging design requests required cleaning up AI-generated content, work that accounted for 60% to 70% of her annual income. But the grind was exhausting. Clients lowballed her;' some AI-generated designs were so flawed that she had to recreate them from scratch and she worried about being complicit in AI-driven copyright infringement. By the end of the year, she began turning those jobs down. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘If he can make money in a tyranny, that’s fine by him’: Francis Fukuyama on Trump, democracy - and changing his mind
data.description: The political thinker became famous for declaring the triumph of liberal democracy. Thirty-seven years on, he explains what he really meant and why he made the rare journey from right to left There are not many public intellectuals who can say they’ve been cited by Capt James T Kirk of the Starship Enterprise, but Francis Fukuyama is one of them. In Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country, William Shatner’s character is in a reflective mood, and speaks to the Klingon chancellor. “Some people think the future means the end of history ,” Kirk muses. “Well, we haven’t run out of history quite yet.” When the film came out in 1991 and in the years that followed, you’d often hear comments like that. They were nods to a thesis so famous it hardly needed spelling out. It debuted in a 15-page essay written by Fukuyama, then a 36-year-old thinktanker, which was published in the National Interest, a right-leaning journal of US foreign policy, in the summer of 1989 . There was a question mark in the title: it was called The End of History?. In book form three years later, it became The End of History and the Last Man. But these were subtleties that, as we shall see, got lost. Continue reading...

data.title: 2,800+ wolves killed, $10M spent, yet 15 caribou herds remain at risk: Is British Columbia targeting wrong?
data.description: British Columbia's ongoing wolf cull initiative aims to support the restoration of caribou populations. Experts contend that habitat destruction, rather than wolf predation, is the primary issue affecting these animals. The provincial government is considering prolonging this contentious ten-year wolf cull for an additional five years, drawing backlash for failing to address habitat degradation. Stakeholder consultations are underway to finalize the decision on extending this program.

Residents are encouraged to verify any official demands through legitimate sources to avoid such traps.

data.title: Fish Removal Reshapes River: Experiment slashed trout, lifted native chub; impact still unclear
data.description: Scientists removed invasive fish from the Colorado River to help native species.  This four-year experiment significantly altered the river's fish population composition.  Rainbow trout numbers dropped dramatically, while native fish showed some signs of recovery.  However, other environmental factors complicated the assessment of the program's success.  Ongoing efforts continue to protect the Grand Canyon's native fish populations.

data.title: Amazon drivers deliver woman’s printer; minutes later, she collapsed and they rushed to help
data.description: Two Amazon delivery drivers in Covington, Kentucky, helped save the life of an 85-year-old woman who collapsed after they delivered a printer to her home. The drivers had carried the printer inside when she invited them to her balcony. She soon felt dizzy and stopped breathing. One driver performed the Heimlich manoeuvre while the other called paramedics, who arrived within five minutes.

This situation reflects broader enforcement issues the IRS faces with conservation easements. The farmer now waits for a resolution, eager to safeguard his family's agricultural heritage.

data.title: Seabiscuit’s California ranch became a conservation haven for wetlands
data.description: Ridgewood Ranch, located in Mendocino County, is celebrated for being the sanctuary where Seabiscuit spent his retirement. Beyond its equestrian legacy, the ranch plays a crucial role in wildlife conservation, as dedicated preservationists have successfully shielded over 4,600 acres from development threats. Conservation easements now protect its key habitats and historic buildings, ensuring that this iconic site continues to support both a legendary sports narrative and a thriving ecosystem.

data.title: A Wyoming ranch was bought for conservation, but cattle stayed to protect it
data.description: A Wyoming ranch proved cattle grazing can protect ecosystems. Conservationists bought Red Canyon Ranch and kept cattle grazing to test coexistence. Managed grazing mimics historical patterns, supporting grasslands and diverse plant communities. This approach informs conservation strategies across the American West today. The ranch serves as a model for balancing agriculture and biodiversity goals.

data.title: A fungus turns beetles into zombies and makes them die on flowers to infect the next generation
data.description: A fungus infects goldenrod soldier beetles, causing them to grip flowers before dying.  After death, the fungus alters their bodies, raising wings between midnight and 7 am.  These changes occur approximately fifteen to twenty-two hours after the beetles have expired.  Infected beetles were found on frost aster and common boneset plants in Arkansas.  Fungal outbreaks primarily occurred during autumn when adult beetles are present.

data.title: ‘Ghost’ green mamba rediscovered decades after its 1885 discovery in São Tomé
data.description: Researchers have made an exciting discovery of a long-lost 1885 green mamba specimen from São Tomé Island, previously thought to be missing. Found within a Polish museum's collection, this specimen enables scientists to revisit its taxonomic classification. With physical traits closely matching the western green mamba, this rediscovery ignites curiosity about the survival status of this snake on its native island.

data.description: A maioria dos políticos lança suas campanhas de um púlpito. Raphaël Glucksmann começou sua candidatura à Presidência da França escalando uma turbina eólica de 80 metros. "Não tenho medo, mal posso esperar para chegar ao topo", disse o candidato, vestido com capacete e arnês. De volta ao solo, ele prometeu uma "revolução ambiental de cem dias" caso seja eleito em 2027 para combater as mudanças climáticas e livrar a França dos combustíveis fósseis. data.title: Vânia Mignone celebra três décadas de arte pop e cores febris em nova exposição

Seus quadros, pintados em cores berrantes sobre placas de MDF, costumam conter expressões como futuro, caos, parto, nós, selva. E elas ainda aparecem nos trabalhos inéditos que ela apresenta na Casa Triângulo, galeria paulistana que a representa há três décadas. A diferença é que, agora, as letras estão confinadas aos quadros. Leia mais (09/03/2026 - 04h00)

data.title: SP e RJ têm a pior percepção de melhoria da educação em 4 anos, segundo pesquisa
data.description: Rio de Janeiro e São Paulo têm a pior percepção da população em relação à melhoria das escolas públicas de seus estados ao longo dos últimos quatro anos, de acordo com a pesquisa "O que a população pensa sobre a educação 2026". Em ambos os casos, 25% dos entrevistados afirmam que a qualidade dessas instituições "piorou" ou "piorou muito" no período. Por outro lado, 38% apontam que a situação "melhorou" ou "melhorou muito" no RJ, enquanto 33% dizem o mesmo do ensino paulista -os percentuais são os mais baixos entre as unidades da federação do país. Leia mais (09/03/2026 - 00h01)

data.title: Semana do Cinema tem filmes por R$ 10, incluindo sessões Imax, em redes de São Paulo
data.description: A semana do cinema começa na próxima quinta (10) e se estende até 16 de setembro com sessões a partir de R$ 10 nas principais redes de cinema de São Paulo . As redes Cine Araújo, Cinemark, Cinesystem, Cinépolis, Moviecom e UCI participam da ação. No período, elas oferecem ingressos por R$ 10 para sessões iniciadas até as 17h e por R$ 12 para exibições nos demais horários, incluindo finais de semana. O desconto não é aplicado em pré-estreias e transmissões de shows. Leia mais (09/02/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Trilha Interparques leva ciclistas por 182km na zona sul de São Paulo
data.description: Esta coluna nunca foi muito de falar de cicloturismo, até porque, confesso: nunca aprendi a andar de bicicleta. Meu negócio é um pé na frente do outro. Eventualmente, um acima do outro numa escalaminhada com a bunda, o chamado quinto apoio, pelo meio. Mas, com a explosão do universo ciclista em vias urbanas e trilhas, resolvi dar uma chance ao esporte, que há tempos não tem mais um espaço específico no jornal. Isto posto, vamos estrear conversando com uma das maiores ativistas do mundo de duas rodas do país, quiçá do universo: Renata Falzoni. Leia mais (09/02/2026 - 23h00)

Ingen annan regering har i modern tid gjort mer för friheten i Sverige, skriver partiledare Simona Mohamsson (L).

data.title: Starkare El Niño än någonsin väcker oro på Afrikas horn

data.title: Inget straffbart i tenniskuppen – Gardell och Rosberg frias

Akcja trwa do 6 września.

data.title: Norové zadrželi ruskou loď, vymáhají miliardy pro Ukrajinu. Pirátství, zuří Moskva
data.description: Norsko v Arktidě zadrželo ruskou loď, aby zajistilo možnost vymáhat náhradu škody ve výši 4,22 miliardy dolarů (přibližně 88,16 miliardy Kč). Mluvčí ruského ministerstva zahraničí to označil za pirátství.

data.title: Nizozemci reagují na nestabilitu. Část zlatých rezerv přesunuli z USA do Londýna
data.description: Nizozemská centrální banka (DNB) přesunula více než čtvrtinu svých zlatých rezerv uložených v USA a Kanadě do Velké Británie. Oznámila to ve čtvrtečním prohlášení s odkazem na obavy z geopolitické nestability. data.title: Už ji nebudu hájit. Ženu viněnou z utýrání jezevčíka náhle opustila advokátka
data.description: Hlavní líčení v případu utýraného jezevčíka v Teplicích se komplikuje. Obžalovaná žena přišla o obhájkyni, jež ji odmítla dál zastupovat. Před soudem vyslovila přání získat nyní bezplatného advokáta. Soud měl v plánu projednat posudek na klíčového svědka – malého synovce obžalované – a možná i vynést verdikt. Místo toho tedy musel s ohledem na okolnosti jednání odročit.

data.description: Na okraji Prostějova se ve středu odpoledne střetl motorový vlak s popelářským vozidlem. Při srážce motorový vůz částečně vykolejil. Zranilo se sedm lidí, tři z nich středně těžce. Doprava na trati byla šest a půl hodiny zastavena. Souhrnné škody byly zatím vyčísleny na zhruba osm milionů korun. Policisté událost vyšetřují pro podezření z trestných činů obecné ohrožení z nedbalosti a těžké ublížení na zdraví z nedbalosti.

data.title: První česká střela s plochou dráhou letu prošla testy a je v hledáčku NATO
data.description: Česká technologická společnost LPP Holding úspěšně dokončila testování první střely s plochou dráhou letu Narwhal, která je schopná zasáhnout cíl na více než 600 kilometrů. A zatímco konstruktéři už pracují na vývoji dalších dvou těžších variant, NATO si vybralo firmu mezi desítku nejlepších inovátorů. Firma také potvrdila, že je připravena relativně rychle spustit masovou výrobu.

data.title: Vláda neuspěla. Šámal zůstane soudcem v kauze Pavlovy kompetenční žaloby
data.description: Pavel Šámal zůstane soudcem zpravodajem v řízení o kompetenční žalobě prezidenta Petra Pavla. Vyloučení Šámala z projednávání a rozhodování navrhla vláda, plénum Ústavního soudu jí však nevyhovělo. V žádném soudním řízení v Česku nelze soudce označit za podjatého jen kvůli jeho postupu v řízení, stojí v usnesení zpřístupněném na webu Ústavního soudu.

data.title: Na staveniště v Mnichově zaútočili žháři. Policie vidí politický motiv
data.description: Staveniště před sídlem technologické firmy v Mnichově se v noci stalo terčem žhářského útoku. Podle mluvčího zemského kriminálního úřadu (LKA) policie případ vyšetřuje jako pokus o útok s politickým motivem. Policie zadržela dva podezřelé Bulhary. Firma Rohde & Schwarz, na kterou útok zjevně mířil, dodává zboží i ozbrojeným silám. Škoda vznikla jen malá, informoval web bavorského rozhlasu BR24.

data.title: Estonský ministr obrany končí kvůli skandálu s koupí munice pro Ukrajinu
data.description: V souvislosti se skandálem kolem objednávek dělostřelecké munice pro Ukrajinu oznámil svou rezignaci estonský ministr obrany Hanno Pevkur. Své rozhodnutí oznámil ve vysílání televizního pořadu Aktuaalne kaamera. „Lídr musí mít jak odvahu, tak úroveň, aby převzal politickou odpovědnost, i když nejde o osobní odpovědnost. Tuto odpovědnost převezmu a premiér bude muset najít nového ministra obrany,“ řekl Pevkur, jenž funkci zastával od roku 2022.

data.title: Motoristé budou jednat s Babišem a Schillerovou, kde chtějí ušetřit v rozpočtu
data.description: Premiér Andrej Babiš musí hasit první větší spor ve vládní koalici. Na jednání za ním a ministryní financí Alenou Schillerovou dorazí šéf Motoristů sobě, ministr zahraničí Petr Macinka, a šéf rozpočtového výboru za Motoristy sobě Vladimír Pikora. Koaličním partnerům ANO vadí navržený schodek rozpočtu na příští rok 389 miliard korun. Považují ho za příliš vysoký a chtějí hledat úspory.

data.title: Vyšel z domu a udeřil do něj blesk. Přesto si sám došel pro pomoc a mluví o zážitku
data.description: Muže cestou k lékaři na newyorském ostrově Staten Island náhle zasáhl blesk, přesto se okamžitě oklepal a sám si došel pro pomoc. data.title: Nový výpočet „superdávky“ zaskočil matky i svobodné. Stovky tisíc lidí přišly o peníze
data.description: Osmadvacetiletá Gabriela žije sama v garsonce v Praze. Aby si bydlení mohla dovolit, dlouhodobě čerpala příspěvek na bydlení. V červenci 2026 požádala o novou takzvanou superdávku. Ta nově nahrazuje kromě příspěvku na bydlení také přídavek na dítě, příspěvek na živobytí a ještě takzvaný doplatek na bydlení. Změnou systému ale žadatelka přišla o značnou část peněz. A není zdaleka jediná.

data.title: EU official says it’s not time to ‘normalize’ Russia at G20 finance talks
data.description:
ASHEVILLE: EU economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis said Tuesday that it is not the time to “normalize” Moscow’s presence at G20 meetings as European leaders pushed back against the Russian finance minister’s attendance at ongoing talks.
	“I think the European position is known,” Dombrovskis told reporters on the sidelines of the US-hosted finance leaders’ gathering in Asheville, North Carolina.
	“We do not think now is the time to normalize Russia” or its presence at such talks, the Latvian official said.

data.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill three in operation to seize Hamas figure: officials

data.title: World leaders need to see rising oceans in Pacific: UN official
data.description:
KOROR: Leaders from the world's top economies should stand on a Pacific atoll to see the reality of record sea level rise, a top UN official said in Palau on Monday.

	Noting last week's deadly floods in Nepal, United Nations Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed said rising seas in the Pacific were the "other side of that story".

	"We do already know that a warming climate is changing the world's ice at extraordinary speeds, not only threatening the communities below glaciers but adding more water to our oceans," she told reporters.

data.title: California lawmakers pass bill allowing people to identify their Jewish ancestry on state forms
data.description:
SACRAMENTO, California: California would allow Jews to voluntarily identify their Jewish heritage on state forms under a bill the state Legislature passed Monday.
	The bill, which lawmakers sent to Gov. Gavin Newsom’s desk, would require state agencies that collect demographic information to add “Jewish” as an option for ethnicity or ancestry. The goal is to give state officials and researchers better data on Jewish Californians, including their unemployment rates and representation in schools.

data.title: Nepal says death toll rises to 987, bringing total killed past 1,000
data.description:
KATMANDU, Nepal: Devastating floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 987 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said Tuesday, taking overall deaths to more than 1,000.

	Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 people were killed in Tibet, bringing the total toll from Wednesday’s disaster to 1,003.

	The number of missing in Nepal dropped to 3,916, as rescue efforts entered a seventh day, and the bodies recovered rose.

	In China, state media say there 546 people missing, taking the overall number of missing to 4,462.

data.title: La FFB et WANAW : l’alliance des guerriers et du fil d’or
data.description:
Il y a des signatures qui ne sont pas de simples paraphes. Il y a des serments.  
 Ce 31 août 2026, dans le recueillement de Bujumbura, la Fédération de Football du Burundi a renouvelé son vœu avec Habte Garment Printing, propriétaire de la marque WANAW. 
 Née en 1948, gardienne des trois couleurs, affiliée à la FIFA, à la CAF et à la CECAFA, la FFB ne confie pas à n’importe qui la tunique de ses fils. Elle la confie à ceux qui savent tailler la dignité dans le tissu.

data.title: Cameroun : le nouvel ambassadeur de l’Union européenne prend fonction à Yaoundé
data.description: © Minrex S.E. Veronika Boskovic Pohar a présenté les copies figurées de ses lettres de créance au ministère des Relations extérieures du Cameroun le mercredi 02 septembre 2026. L'ambassadeur désigné, chef de la délégation de l'Union européenne au Cameroun a présenté mercredi, les copies figurées de ses lettres de créances au ministre délégué auprès du ministre des Relations extérieures chargé de la coopération avec le Commonwealth, Felix Mbayu. C'était au cours d'une cérémonie qui a donné l'opportunité aux deux personnalités de revisiter la coopération entre le Cameroun et l'Union européenne et d'aborder la situation socio-politique du Cameroun. Successeur de S.E. Jean Marc Châtaigner arrivé en fin de mission à la fin du mois d'août dernier, le nouvel ambassadeur a exprimé sa détermination à collaborer avec les autorités camerounaises en vue d'atteindre des objectifs qui lui ont été fixés. Diplomate de carrière, elle a, avant sa désignation pour le Cameroun, servi en qualité de chef de la délégation de l'Union européenne en Afghanistan depuis le 1er septembre 2024. Elle totalise 20 ans d'expérience dans le domaine de la politique sécuritaire, des relations multilatérales ainsi que de la politique extérieure de l'Union européenne. Elle cumule des formations et l’expérience dans la gestion des crises, les relations consulaires, la coordination de la défense. Entre septembre 2020 et août 2024, Veronika a servi comme ambassadeur représentant du Comité politique et sécuritaire à la représentation permanente de l'Union européenne en Slovénie. Dans le même pays, elle a travaillé comme adjointe au chef de la mission de Slovénie en France et au Royaume du Maroc. Juriste et diplomate slovène, Veronika Boskovic Pohar a été désignée il y a trois mois à la tête de la délégation de l'Union européenne au Cameroun. Cet article Cameroun : le nouvel ambassadeur de l’Union européenne prend fonction à Yaoundé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Coopération militaire : Washington et Yaoundé sécurisent la flotte C-208
data.description: © DR Le Groupe militaire américain (MILGP) et l'armée de l'air camerounaise ont réalisé le 1er septembre 2026 un inventaire conjoint de pièces de rechange pour avions C-208 d'une valeur de 254 906 227 FCFA, confirmant l'engagement américain dans la lutte antiterroriste au Cameroun. La coopération militaire américano-camerounaise se renforce. Le 1er septembre 2026, " le Groupe militaire américain au Cameroun (MILGP) s'est associé à l'armée de l'air camerounaise pour réaliser un inventaire conjoint des pièces de rechange des avions C-208. Une opération évaluée à 254 906 227 FCFA, soit environ 447 580,19 dollars, qui témoigne de l'investissement soutenu du gouvernement américain dans les capacités opérationnelles du Cameroun. Au-delà de l'aspect logistique, cet inventaire vise à garantir le maintien en condition opérationnelle des moyens aériens essentiels dans la lutte contre le terrorisme. Les C-208, appareils clés pour la surveillance et le transport tactique, restent ainsi pleinement mobilisables. Un geste qui illustre la solidité du partenariat stratégique entre Washington et Yaoundé face aux défis sécuritaires régionaux. Cet article Coopération militaire : Washington et Yaoundé sécurisent la flotte C-208 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Recherche en santé : le Cameroun se projette avec un plan quinquennal de 2,533 milliards de F
data.description: © DR Le Plan stratégique national de la recherche en santé (Psnrs) 2026-2030 a été présenté le 1er septembre 2026 à Yaoundé. Il entre dans sa phase de mise en œuvre. Un nouvel outil d'aide à la décision et d'amélioration de l'action sanitaire fait son entrée dans le dispositif existant. Le Plan stratégique national de santé publique (Psnrs) vise à renforcer la recherche en santé et mieux intégrer les connaissances produites dans la prise de décisions. A travers cet outil, il est question de veiller à l'utilisation des connaissances issues des recherches dans la formulation et la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques. D'un budget estimatif de 2,533 milliards de FCFA pour sa mise en œuvre, le plan est centré sur plusieurs axes. Ce sont le renforcement de la gouvernance, de l'éthique de la recherche, de l'utilisation des données probantes dans la prise de décision. À cela s'ajoutent l'institutionnalisation d'une culture de recherche dans le système de santé et de la mobilisation durable des financements, indique le ministère de la Santé publique. Ce plan apporte des innovations dans le système de recherche en santé déjà existant. Il entend intégrer d'autres niveaux de structures à partir desquels la recherche pourra partir. Sans toutefois exclure les administrations centrales, les universités et instituts spécialisés, il y associe des réalités observées dans les régions, les districts de santé, les formations sanitaires et les communautés. Avec ce plan, les districts de santé pourront mener des observations, innover, apprendre et faire la recherche opérationnelle, toujours d’après la même source. L'entrée en phase de mise en mise en œuvre de ce plan coïncide avec le lancement officiel du Centre de documentation numérique du secteur santé. Bibliothèque virtuelle dans le domaine, il va contribuer à centraliser, préserver organiser et à rendre plus accessible les rapports, études, documents techniques et autres productions scientifiques. Lance le 1 er septembre 2026 à Yaoundé, Les professionnels de santé, les chercheurs, les décideurs et autres acteurs du secteur de la santé peuvent y accéder via l'adresse cdnss-minsante.cm . Cet article Recherche en santé : le Cameroun se projette avec un plan quinquennal de 2,533 milliards de F est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : la campagne « Santé gratuite pour tous » fait son bilan dans l’Extrême-Nord
data.description: © DR Au terme de la campagne de santé déployée dans des aires de santé de la région de l'Extrême-Nord par le ministre de la Santé publique, le bilan fait état de plusieurs dizaines de cas de chirurgies effectuées. La clôture de la campagne « Santé gratuite pour tous » a lieu ce 02 septembre 2026 au cours d'une cérémonie au stade municipal de Mokolo. Au bout d'une semaine d'intervention dans les formations sanitaires, 61 cas de fistules obstétricales ont été pris en charge à Mokolo, chef-lieu du département de Mayo-Tsanaga. Les patients sont issus de la région, mais aussi d’autres zones comme Bertoua dans la région de l'Est, Yaoundé dans le Centre ou encore du Tchad et du Nigeria. Sur l'ensemble des patients, 57 cas de fistules ont été opérés avec succès, 11 patients sont sortis d'hospitalisation, 46 patients sont encore en salle d'hospitalisation. Quatre opérations chirurgicales étaient programmés le 1er septembre. Ce 02 septembre marque la clôture de la campagne. Mais, de passage pour l’evaluation de la campagne à Mokolo, le ministre Malachie Manaouda a rassuré que la campagne va se poursuivre et les patients restants continueront d’être pris en charge. La gratuité aussi restera jusqu'à la fin de la campagne. Le ministre a par ailleurs rassuré qu'il va relever le plateau technique, mettre à la disposition de l'Hôpital central de Mokolo une ressource humaine de qualité. data.title: Mombasa 2026 : l’ANOR décroche un Award de l’excellence
data.description: © DR Récompensée pour la qualité de son engagement au service de la normalisation en Afrique, l'ANOR s'est illustrée à la 32e Assemblée Générale de l'ARSO à Mombasa. Un Award de l'excellence qui consacre le leadership du Cameroun sur le marché africain. Bilan positif pour le Cameroun à Mombasa. Du 25 au 29 août 2026, la délégation camerounaise a pris part à la 32e Assemblée Générale de l’Organisation Africaine de Normalisation (ARSO) au Kenya, axée sur la normalisation, l’évaluation de la conformité et la promotion du commerce intra-africain. Les travaux ont mis en avant l’importance du leadership des États dans l’adoption des normes africaines harmonisées. Avec désormais 2 742 normes, l’ARSO poursuit son ambition : « Une norme, un test, un certificat accepté partout et par tous ». Le leadership du Cameroun, aux côtés des États ayant déjà lancé l’ARSO Mark, a été salué. Conduite par M. MBAMBA Alain Michel, représentant de Madame le Directeur Général, la délégation composée de M. CHESAMI, CT1, de Mme AFANE ETOUNOU DANIELLE épouse NDONGO et de M. NDEMBIYEMBE YVAN, s’est distinguée par la qualité de ses interventions. Point culminant : l’ANOR a reçu un AWARD de l’excellence, récompensant son engagement au service de la qualité. Une distinction qui consacre l’Agence et renforce sa visibilité sur la scène internationale. Cet article Mombasa 2026 : l’ANOR décroche un Award de l’excellence est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : plus de 169 200 jeunes inscrits sur les listes électorales en 2026
data.description: © DR La proportion des jeunes inscrits sur les listes électorales au cours de la campagne de révision 2026 est le double du nombre d'adultes pointés. Le chiffre semble être révélateur à plus d’un titre. Les chiffres rendus publics par la direction générale des élections au terme de la campagne de révision des listes électorales couvrant la période de début janvier à fin août 2026 sont parlants. Ils révèlent l'engouement d'une bonne partie de la jeunesse à participer aux affaires politiques du pays. D'après ces chiffres, 169 225 jeunes, dont 103 230 jeunes hommes et 65 995 jeunes femmes ont été inscrits au cours de la campagne 2026, contre 83 605 adultes de plus de 35 ans. Soit un taux d'inscription des jeunes de moins de 35 ans équivalent à 66,93% contre 33,07% pour les adultes de plus de 35 ans. La proportion des jeunes indique en filigrane le poids que ces derniers peuvent peser dans le fichier électoral et sur les résultats d'une élection. Leur nombre est le double de celui des adultes en raison du fait que dans cette tranche se trouvent les jeunes qui viennent d'atteindre la majorité électorale fixée à 20 ans et ceux qui, l'ayant atteint depuis quelques années, veulent s'intéresser à la politique. En outre, cette tranche est parmi les plus denses au sein de la population camerounaise. Elle est une composante de la tranche de 15 à 35 ans qui constitue une masse de 35 à 36% de la population du Cameroun, d'après l'Institut national de la statique. Avec les femmes et les personnes vivant avec un handicap, la jeunesse est l'une des cibles privilégiées d'Elecam. Les campagnes de communication incitant les citoyens à s'inscrire sur les listes électorales déployées ces deniers mois par Elecam ont ciblé ces catégories sociales, qui manifestent souvent des réticences face aux affaires politiques. Ces réticences s'expliquent par le fait des discours selon lesquels les postes politiques sont en grande majorité attribués aux hommes expérimentés, tandis que les jeunes et les femmes accompagnent ces derniers. Le désintérêt des jeunes s'expliquait aussi en partie par un autre discours des aînés incitant à la peur en faisant croire aux jeunes que la politique est dangereuse. Pourtant, grâce à l'argument du nombre, la jeunesse peut obliger les candidats aux élections à se plier à leurs exigences au moment des consultations électorales. Elle peut exercer son influence sur le choix des candidats en privilégiant ceux qui présentent des projets favorables à la résolution de leurs problèmes. Il s'agit en particulier de la réduction du chômage qui touche environ 35% des jeunes de 15 à 35 ans en 2024 selon les données de la Banque mondiale, du sous-emploi, des difficultés d'accès à la terre, des difficultés d'accès aux sphères de prise de décision, des mauvaises conditions de vie, et bien d'autres. À voir l'initiative des jeunes qui veulent se lancer à la conquête des sièges au sein des conseils municipaux et à l'Assemblée nationale en 2027, les chiffres de la campagne de révision 2026 indiquent une certaine tendance à la prise de conscience d'une jeunesse décidé à prendre les commandes pour changer leur pays. Cet article Cameroun : plus de 169 200 jeunes inscrits sur les listes électorales en 2026 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Comment vivre avec une personne colérique et impulsive ?
data.description: Vivre avec une personne colérique cause souvent le stress et l’angoisse dans son entourage, selon nos sources. Pour un fait banal, monsieur ou madame s’emporte, hausse le ton et met les autres mal à l’aise. Certains deviennent agressifs et débordent jusqu’à insulter, frapper ou casser les objets à la maison. D’après les experts, une personne colérique accepte mal la contradiction et reconnait difficilement ses torts ou ses erreurs.

data.title: Un projet anti-érosion de 1,5 million USD ravive l’espoir au Camp Munganga à Kinshasa
data.description: Les travaux de construction d’un collecteur d’eau sont en cours au Camp Munganga, dans la commune de Ngaliema, à Kinshasa, pour lutter contre l’érosion qui affecte cette partie de la capitale depuis quelques mois. Financé par le gouvernement congolais à hauteur de près de 1,5 million de dollars américains, le chantier est exécuté par l’Office des voiries et drainage (OVD). Il fait notamment suite aux plaidoyers menés par l’ONGD COTENEPROD.

data.title: Venezuela firma acuerdos energéticos con Estados Unidos y petroleras
data.description: El Gobierno de la presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, firmó este miércoles acuerdos energéticos con una delegación de EE.UU. encabezada por el secretario de Energía, Chris Wright, a pocos días de que se conociera el pacto petrolero con Washington. “Hoy es un día histórico en la transformación de Venezuela”, afirmó Wright. The post Venezuela firma acuerdos energéticos con Estados Unidos y petroleras first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Capturan al hermano de “El Diablo” con droga en Sulaco, Yoro
data.description: Sulaco, Yoro. Patricio Ferrera Rodas, de 40 años, hermano de "El Diablo" y señalado por las autoridades como presunto colaborador del grupo delictivo denominado “Cártel del Diablo”, fue capturado este miércoles en el barrio El Centro de Sulaco, Yoro, en posesión de unos 40 envoltorios de supuesto clorhidrato de cocaína. La captura fue ejecutada por agentes de la Dirección Nacional Policial Antidrogas (DNPA), quienes ubicaron al sospechoso cuando se desplazaba a bordo de una mototaxi. Durante el registro, los agentes inspeccionaron una mochila que llevaba Ferrera Rodas y encontraron aproximadamente 40 envoltorios con polvo blanco, supuesto clorhidrato de cocaína, además de un teléfono celular. Según los registros policiales, el detenido cuenta con antecedentes por tráfico ilícito de drogas y portación ilegal de arma de fuego de uso permitido. Las investigaciones también establecen su presunta vinculación como colaborador de la estructura criminal denominada “Cártel del Diablo”. Ferrera Rodas será remitido al Ministerio Público, donde deberá responder por suponerlo responsable de los delitos de tráfico ilícito de drogas y asociación para delinquir.
